$comment: Phase 0.4 gate-4 DoD step 5: machine-readable rubric for embedder Full-tier re-eval. R2 (expanded schema; runner evaluates flip rules directly) + G2 (label schema plus labeler instructions embedded). Post-hoc-edit-locked per ADR-0030 §Rubric-lock.

co_residency.$comment: Enforced by the runner before each embedder cell starts. Verified via the /v1/models 404 check on each server after teardown.
before_each_embedder_cell: stop coder vLLM container on :8501 (docker rm -f)
stop planner llama.cpp server on GPU (systemctl or pkill by process name)
confirm no GPU VRAM in use (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader,nounits < 500)

harness_flags.note: All embedder cells run llama.cpp with -ngl 0 (pure CPU) per ADR-0017 amend #3.

candidate_pool.$comment: Anchored to bench/candidates/embedder-full-pool.json; pinned here for provenance.

metrics.$comment: Composite exactly as specified in ADR-0030 §K3.

nDCG@10.note: Uses 0-3 grades directly as gain values.

Recall@1.note: Top-1 must be a hit at grade >= 1.

metrics.$primary_key_rule: P1: (repo, source_file_path, line_range). Chunker-agnostic — the same qrel file is used to score both H1 and H2 cells. Runner maps each retrieved chunk back to its (repo, path, line_range) footprint and matches against qrel primary keys.

primary_key.$comment: P1 chunker-agnostic key. Runner must extract this tuple from every retrieved chunk before scoring.
primary_key.line_range_format: inclusive-inclusive integer pair '[start, end]' referring to the source file's line numbers at the pinned snapshot SHA
primary_key.chunk_to_key_mapping: runner MUST store per-chunk source metadata at index-build time; matching is exact-string on repo + path, and 'line_range covers or is covered by' semantics on line_range (any chunk whose lines fully contain OR are fully contained by a qrel line_range is considered a match)

grading.$comment: G2: label schema + labeler instructions in one place. Perplexity-Max labelers read this section verbatim at labeling session start.

meanings.0: Not relevant. Chunk does not answer the query or is off-topic.
meanings.1: Marginally relevant. Chunk touches the query topic but doesn't answer it (e.g., mentions the concept in passing, refers to a related but distinct construct).
meanings.2: Relevant. Chunk substantively answers the query but is missing at least one meaningful detail the querent would want (e.g., mentions the port but not its adapter; describes the ADR title but not its decision).
meanings.3: Directly relevant. Chunk is the answer or a canonical component of the answer (e.g., contains the exact function definition asked about, or the ADR body whose title matches the query intent).

meanings.primary: The canonical answer chunk(s). A query typically has 1-3 primary chunks. A code query's primary is the def/class or the specific method body being asked about. A docs query's primary is the ADR/section that directly resolves the query.
meanings.secondary: Chunks that partially answer, provide context, or are near-duplicates of the primary. May have grade 2 or 3.

role.constraint: Every query MUST have at least one primary chunk with grade 3. Queries whose corpus has no grade-3 answer are excluded from the qrel set (logged separately as 'unanswerable_at_pinned_snapshot').

labeler_instructions_verbatim: Read the query. Consider what a natural agent — coder for code queries, planner/PM for docs queries — would want to retrieve.

For each pooled candidate chunk (union of top-20 across all 12 cells), assign a grade 0-3 using the definitions above. Do NOT peek at which cell retrieved it before grading — labels must be independent of retrieval source to prevent bias.
Assign role=primary to the 1-3 chunks that are the query's canonical answer. Everything else that's non-zero grade is role=secondary.
If a chunk covers the answer but at a different granularity than another chunk (e.g., a whole file that contains the specific function), grade both, but pick the more specific one as primary.
If a chunk contains the answer AND a lot of noise, prefer grade 2 over grade 3 (the retrieval is fine but the presented context is bloated).
For docs queries asking 'which ADR governs X': the ADR title-and-decision section is grade 3 primary; the ADR references in the spec §17 table are grade 2 secondary; unrelated ADRs are grade 0.

For code queries asking 'where is X defined': the def line ± its body is grade 3 primary; import statements or references are grade 2 secondary; documentation of the same construct is grade 1 (unless the query explicitly asks about docs).

If a query is genuinely unanswerable from the pinned corpus, mark it 'unanswerable_at_pinned_snapshot' in a separate field. Do NOT invent grade-3 labels to satisfy the 'at least one primary' constraint.
Labeling is done ACROSS the pooled union — same chunks may be pooled from multiple cells. Each unique (query, chunk) pair is labeled exactly once.

labeling_session_plan.sessions: 2-4 sessions per user preference GL2, split by block (code/docs) and/or by chunker family (H1/H2) to reduce fatigue-induced drift
labeling_session_plan.budget_per_session: 150-300 label decisions max; if larger, split further
labeling_session_plan.drift_check: each session's first 10 queries are re-labeled at the end of that session; if any label changes, halt and re-open the drift-detection ADR

reversal_criteria.$comment: V3 + W3 verbatim from ADR-0030 §V3-W3. Runner evaluates these as boolean predicates after block-macro composites are computed. Boundary → incumbent per ADR-0030 policy.
reversal_criteria.boundary_policy: if any predicate below is ambiguous (numeric boundary case at 3-point threshold, or 5-point regression at exactly 5), the incumbent wins

confirm_incumbent_4b_q8_if.$comment: Any single clause fires → CONFIRM incumbent (4B-Q8_0). Evaluated first.

any_of.predicate: not any(flip_gate_passes_on_block['code', c] for c in {8b_q6k, 0_6b_q8})
not any(flip_gate_passes_on_block['docs', c] for c in {8b_q6k, 0_6b_q8})

flip_to_8b_q6k_if.$comment: ALL five clauses must fire → FLIP to 8B-Q6_K.

all_of.predicate: for each metric m in {nDCG@10, Recall@10, MRR@10, Recall@1}, and each block b: block_metric[b, m, 4b_q8] - block_metric[b, m, 8b_q6k] <= 5
for each metric m and each block b: block_metric[b, m, 4b_q8] - block_metric[b, m, 8b_q6k] <= 2 OR the composite gain on that block is >= 5 (offset clause)

flip_to_8b_q6k_if.note: single_metric_loss_greater_2 has an offset clause: a >5 composite gain on the block absorbs one >2 metric loss on the same block. Runner logs the offset use for ADR-0031 audit.

flip_to_0_6b_q8_if.$comment: ALL five clauses must fire → FLIP to 0.6B-Q8_0.

all_of.predicate: for each metric m in {nDCG@10, Recall@10, MRR@10, Recall@1}, and each block b: block_metric[b, m, 4b_q8] - block_metric[b, m, 0_6b_q8] <= 5
for each metric m and each block b: block_metric[b, m, 4b_q8] - block_metric[b, m, 0_6b_q8] <= 2 (no offset clause on downsize — strict)

flip_to_0_6b_q8_if.note: downsize does NOT get the composite-offset clause on single_metric_loss; the tighter requirement reflects that 'save resources at all costs' can't override retrieval loss.

evaluation_order: 1. Compute per-cell metrics (nDCG@10, Recall@10, MRR@10, Recall@1) using qrels.
2. Compute block_metric[block, metric, candidate] = mean across chunker variants (H1 and H2 average).
3. Compute block_macro[block, candidate] via the primary_composite formula.
4. Compute overall_macro[candidate] = mean(block_macro[code, c], block_macro[docs, c]).
5. Evaluate confirm_incumbent_4b_q8_if — if any clause fires, verdict = CONFIRM incumbent. Skip other predicates.

6. If not confirmed: evaluate flip_to_8b_q6k_if AND flip_to_0_6b_q8_if. If exactly one passes → that verdict. If both pass → 8b wins (tie-break on higher block_macro sum). If neither passes → verdict = CONFIRM incumbent (fallback per V3 boundary policy).
7. If per-block split is possible (one candidate passes W3 on code but not docs, or vice versa) → verdict = INTERMEDIATE, follow-up ADR required for per-block routing.

gate_4_dod_full: step_6_qrels_labeled_and_locked:  PENDING (per GL2, 2-4 Perplexity-Max sessions; ends with QRELS.locked.sha256)
step_9_ADR-0031_verdict_filed:    PENDING (runner evaluates reversal_criteria + records verdict; ADR-0030 Ratifies at this point OR gets amended-then-ratified if the reversal fires)
